1947.subject: Zoology
1947.text:
Assertion : Inflammation of a skeletal joint may immobilize the movements of the joint.
Reason : Uric acid crystals in the joint cavity and ossification of articular cartilage lead to this.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
1947.sol:
Inflammation is a process in which the body's WBCs and the chemicals released into the blood or the affected tissue to protect us from infection and foreign substances such as bacteria and viruses. This releases of chemicals increases the blood flow to the area of injury or infection. Inflammation is characterized by redness, swollen joint that is warm to touch, joint pain, joint stiffness \& loss of joint function.
The increase number of cells and inflammatory substances within the joint causes irritation, wearing down of cartilage (cushions at the end of bones) and swelling of the joint lining. Inflammation of one or more joint results in arthritis. When there is a deposition of uric acid and crystals of sodium urates in the joints it will lead to gout arthritis. Uric acids is the end metabolism products of nitrogen containing purine nucleic acid. Gout generally affects one or two joints only. It is very painful particularly at night, and makes movement difficult. Gout generally affects great toe.

2710.text: Wurtz reaction of bromoethane gives \(n\)-butane. Sodium salt of \(X\) on heating with sodalime also results in \(n\)-butane. Compound \(X\) is

In Wurtz reaction, two molecules of bromoethane react with 2 molecules of sodium to form \(n\)-butane.
\begin{aligned}$\mathrm{CH}_{3}- \mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na}+\mathrm{Br}$-$\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ \\
-2 $\mathrm{NaBr}$ \longrightarrow $\mathrm{CH}_{3}- \mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$\end{aligned} \)
\(n\)-butane can also be obtain when sodium salt$ of $pentanoic acid \((X)\) gets heated with sodalime. The reaction is given as under :
\(\underset{(X)}{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\left(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\right)_3 \mathrm{COOH}}$\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOH}}\)
\(\underset{\text{ Sodium salt }}{\mathrm{CH}_{3}  \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CH}_{2}  \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COONa}} $\xrightarrow{$\mathrm{NaOH}$+\mathrm{CaO} \text{ (Sodalime) }} \underset{\text{n-butane}}{\mathrm{CH}_{3}  \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CH}_{2}  \mathrm{CH}_{3}}+\mathrm{Na}_{2}  \mathrm{CO}_{3}\)
Hence, \(X\) is \(\mathrm{CH}_{3}  \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{CH}_{2}  \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{COOH}\).

& \Rightarrow $\text{ at }$A=3 $\pi$R^2, $\text{ maximum volume }$\\
& A=3 $\pi$R^2=2 $\pi$R H+$\pi$R^2 \\
& \Rightarrow R=H
\end{aligned}

8151.text: Solve the differential equation given below $\frac{x d y}{d x}=$ y+$\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$
8151.sol:
Given differential equation $\begin{aligned}
\quad x \frac{d y}{d x}& =y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}& =\frac{y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}{x}
\end{aligned}$ Now, put $y=v \cdot x$
\therefore \quad $\frac{d y}{d x}=$ v+x $\frac{d v}{d x}$ On doing substitution, we get $\begin{aligned}& v+x \frac{d v}{d x}= v+\sqrt{1+v^2}\\
\Rightarrow & \int \frac{d v}{\sqrt{1+v^2}}=\int \frac{d x}{x}\\
\Rightarrow & \log _{\ell} C+\log _{\ell}\left(\sqrt{1+v^2}+ v\right)=\log _{\ell} x \\
\Rightarrow & \log\left[\left( y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\right) C\right]=2 \log _{\ell} x \\
\Rightarrow & x²=C\left[ y+\sqrt{y^2+x^2}\right]
\end{aligned}$ Hence, option (1) is correct.

11268.text: If $\alpha$ is a common root of $x^2-5 x+\lambda=0$ and $x^2-8 x-2 \lambda=0(\lambda \neq 0)$ and $\beta, \gamma$ are the other roots of them, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\lambda=$

Now, $\alpha, \beta$ are roots of $x^2-5 x+(-6)=0\Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=5 \Rightarrow \beta=-1$
And, $\alpha, \gamma$ are roots of $x^2-8 x+12=0\Rightarrow \alpha+\gamma=8 \Rightarrow \gamma=2$
So, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\lambda=6-1+2-6=1$.

$= \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)}{2 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)\left(1 + 2 \cdot 4\right)}{3 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{3} - \ldots \ldots$

$= \left[1\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)}{2 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)\left(1 + 2 \cdot 4\right)}{3 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{3} - \ldots \ldots\right] . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, we know that

${\left(1 + x\right)}^{- \dfrac{p}{q}} = 1 - p\left(\dfrac{x}{q}\right) + \dfrac{p\left(p + q\right)}{2 !}{\left(\dfrac{x}{q}\right)}^{2} - \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots$

Therefore, from $\left(i\right)$, we have

$= \left[1\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)}{2 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)\left(1 + 2 \cdot 4\right)}{3 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{3} - \ldots \ldots\right]$

$= 1 - \left[1 - 1\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)}{2 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(1 + 4\right)\left(1 + 2 \cdot 4\right)}{3 !}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{3} + \ldots \ldots\right]$

Comparing with the above standard series, we get

$p = 1, \dfrac{x}{q} = \dfrac{1}{4}, q = 4 ⇒ x = 1$

Therefore,

${\left(1 + x\right)}^{- \dfrac{p}{q}} = {\left(1 + 1\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}} = {2}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}$

Therefore, required sum is

$= \left(1 - {2}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}\right)$

$= \left(\dfrac{2\dfrac{1}{4} - 1}{{2}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}}\right)$

19518.subject: Chemistry
19518.text: Which of the following is a false statement?
options: Methoxymethane has higher boiling point than ethanol.
Alcohols are more soluble is water than hydracarbons of comparable molecular mass.
ortho-and para-nitrophenols are more acidic than phenols.
Phenol is more acidic than alcohol.
19518.sol:
Ethanol (C_{2}H_{5}OH$) exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding due to the presence of the polar -OH group, which leads to a significantly higher boiling point compared to methoxymethane (CH_{3}OCH_{3}$), which is an ether and lacks such hydrogen bonding. Therefore, the statement that methoxymethane has a higher boiling point than ethanol is false.

Alcohols are capable of forming hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making them more soluble in water than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass, which are non-polar. This statement is true.

The nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) is an electron-withdrawing group that stabilizes the phenoxide ion through both inductive and resonance effects. This stabilization increases the acidity of ortho- and para-nitrophenols compared to phenol. This statement is true.

Phenol is more acidic than alcohols because the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton is resonance-stabilized by the benzene ring, whereas the alkoxide ion formed from an alcohol is not stabilized by resonance. This statement is true.

Answer: Methoxymethane has higher boiling point than ethanol.

19912.text: A newly prepared radioactive nuclide has a decay constant of $6.93 \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. What is the half-life of the nuclide?
19912.sol:
The relationship between the half-life $T_{1/2}$ and the decay constant $\lambda$ of a radioactive substance is given by the formula:

$T_{1/2} = \dfrac{\ln(2)}{\lambda}$

Given the decay constant $\lambda = 6.93 \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$ and using the approximation $\ln(2) \approx 0.693$, we substitute these values into the formula:

$T_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93}$

$T_{1/2} = 0.1 \mathrm{ s}$

Answer: $0.1 \mathrm{ s}$

20390.text:
The number of grams of bromine that will completely react with 5 g of pentene is:
[Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Br}=80 \mathrm{u}$ ]
20390.sol:
The chemical formula for pentene is $C_{5}H_{10}$. The reaction of pentene with bromine is an addition reaction:

$C_{5}H_{10} + Br_{2} \rightarrow C_{5}H_{10}Br_{2}$

The molar mass of pentene (C_{5}H_{10}$) is 5 \times 12 + 10 \times 1 = 70$ g/mol.

The molar mass of bromine (Br_{2}$) is 2 \times 80 = 160$ g/mol.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, 1 mole of pentene reacts with 1 mole of bromine. Therefore, 70 g of pentene reacts with 160 g of bromine.

For 5 g of pentene, the mass of bromine required is:

Mass of $Br_{2} = \dfrac{160}{70} \times 5 = \dfrac{800}{70} = \dfrac{80}{7} \approx 11.428$ g.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the value is 11.4 g.

Answer: 11.4 g

21162.subject: Mathematics
21162.text: The conjugate of the multiplicative inverse of the complex number $z = \dfrac{1 + 7i}{3 + i}$ is:
21162.sol:
$z = \dfrac{1 + 7i}{3 + i}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$z = \dfrac{(1 + 7i)(3 - i)}{(3 + i)(3 - i)}$

$z = \dfrac{3 - i + 21i - 7i^2}{3^2 - i^2}$

$z = \dfrac{3 + 20i + 7}{9 + 1}$

$z = \dfrac{10 + 20i}{10} = 1 + 2i$

The multiplicative inverse of $z$ is $\dfrac{1}{z}$:

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1}{1 + 2i}$

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1 - 2i}{(1 + 2i)(1 - 2i)}$

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1 - 2i}{1^2 + 2^2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{2}{5}i$

The conjugate of the multiplicative inverse is:

$\overline{\left(\dfrac{1}{z}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5}i$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5}i$

21773.subject: Mathematics
21773.text:
$\text{ If the matrix } A=\left(\begin{array}{cc}
1 & -1 \\
-1 & 1
\end{array}\right) \text{ then } A^{n+1}=$
21773.sol:
Given $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Calculate $A^2$:

$A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1+1 & -1-1 \\ -1-1 & 1+1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 \end{pmatrix} = 2 \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = 2A$.

Calculate $A^3$:

$A^3 = A^2 \cdot A = (2A) \cdot A = 2A^2 = 2(2A) = 2^2 A$.

By induction, assume $A^k = 2^{k-1} A$.

Then $A^{k+1} = A^k \cdot A = (2^{k-1} A) \cdot A = 2^{k-1} A^2 = 2^{k-1} (2A) = 2^k A$.

Thus, $A^n = 2^{n-1} A$ for $n \ge 1$.

Substituting $n+1$ for $n$, we get $A^{n+1} = 2^{(n+1)-1} A = 2^n A$.

Therefore, $A^{n+1} = 2^n \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Answer: $2^n\left(\begin{array}{cc} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{array}\right)$

21775.text:
$If \left[\begin{array}{lll}
1 & x & 1
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 3 & 2 \\
2 & 5 & 1 \\
15 & 3 & 2
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}
1 \\
2 \\
x
\end{array}\right]=[0]
$ then x is equal to
21775.sol:
Perform the matrix multiplication in two steps. First, multiply the row matrix by the $3 \times 3$ matrix:

\begin{bmatrix} 1 & x & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \\ 15 & 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 + 2x + 15 & 3 + 5x + 3 & 2 + x + 2 \end{bmatrix} = $\begin{bmatrix} 16 + 2x & 6 + 5x & 4 + x \end{bmatrix}$

Now, multiply this result by the column matrix:

\begin{bmatrix} 16 + 2x & 6 + 5x & 4 + x \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ x \end{bmatrix} = [0]$

$(16 + 2x)(1) + (6 + 5x)(2) + (4 + x)(x) = 0$

16 + 2x + 12 + 10x + 4x + x^2 = 0$

$x^2 + 16x + 28 = 0$

Factor the quadratic equation:

$(x + 14)(x + 2) = 0$

Therefore, $x = -14$ or $x = -2$.

Answer: $-2,-14$

22182.text: If the line $\dfrac{1-x}{-3}=y=\dfrac{z+2}{2}$ is perpendicular to the line $\dfrac{3 x-1}{2 b}=3-y=\dfrac{z-1}{a}$, then find the value of $3 a+3 b$
22182.sol:
The first line is given by $\dfrac{x-1}{3} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z+2}{2}$. The direction vector of this line is $\vec{v_1} = 3\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The second line is given by $\dfrac{3x-1}{2b} = \dfrac{y-3}{-1} = \dfrac{z-1}{a}$. Rewriting this in standard form $\dfrac{x - 1/3}{2b/3} = \dfrac{y-3}{-1} = \dfrac{z-1}{a}$. The direction vector of this line is $\vec{v_2} = \dfrac{2b}{3}\hat{i} - 1\hat{j} + a\hat{k}$.

Since the lines are perpendicular, the dot product of their direction vectors must be zero: $\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2} = 0$.

$(3)\left(\dfrac{2b}{3}\right) + (1)(-1) + (2)(a) = 0$.

$2b - 1 + 2a = 0$.

$2a + 2b = 1$.

We need to find the value of $3a + 3b$.

$3(a + b) = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

22670.subject: Physics
22670.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of a neutron having kinetic energy 0.025 eV is $\lambda$. If the kinetic energy of the neutron is reduced to $\dfrac{0.025 \mathrm{eV}}{8}$, its de-Broglie wavelength will be:
22670.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of a particle with mass $m$ and kinetic energy $K$ is given by the relation $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$.

For the initial state, the wavelength is $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(0.025 \text{ eV})}}$.

When the kinetic energy is reduced to $K' = \dfrac{0.025 \text{ eV}}{8}$, the new wavelength $\lambda'$ is given by $\lambda' = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m \times \dfrac{0.025 \text{ eV}}{8}}}$.

Simplifying the expression for $\lambda'$:

$\lambda' = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{\dfrac{2m(0.025 \text{ eV})}{8}}} = \sqrt{8} \times \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(0.025 \text{ eV})}}$.

Since $\sqrt{8} =2\sqrt{2}, we have \lambda' = 2\sqrt{2} \lambda$.

Answer: $2 \sqrt{2} \lambda$

22679.text: The velocity of an electron so that its momentum is equal to that of a photon of wavelength $660 \mathrm{ nm}$ is
22679.sol:
The momentum of a photon is given by $p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$.

Given $\lambda = 660 \text{ nm} = 660 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.

The momentum of an electron is $p = mv$. Equating the two:

$mv = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$

$v = \dfrac{h}{m \lambda}$

Substituting the values $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$, $m = 9.1 imes 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$, and $\lambda = 660 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$:

$v = \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{(9.1 \times 10^{-31}) \times (660 \times 10^{-9})}$

$v = \dfrac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{6006 \times 10^{-40}}$

$v = \dfrac{6.626}{6006} \times 10^{6} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

$v \approx 0.001103 \times 10^{6} \text{ m s}^{-1} = 1103 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Using $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$ for approximation:

$v = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 660 \times 10^{-9}} = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{6006 \times 10^{-40}} = \dfrac{6.6}{6006} \times 10^{6} \approx 1098.9 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

This value is approximately $1098 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $1098 \mathrm{ ms} ^{-1}$

22909.subject: Physics
22909.text: A satellite is revolving around the earth in a circular orbit with kinetic energy of $1.69 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{ J}$. The additional kinetic energy required for just escaping into the outer space is
22909.sol:
For a satellite in a circular orbit of radius $r$ around the earth of mass $M$, the gravitational potential energy is $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ and the kinetic energy is $K = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$.

The total mechanical energy of the satellite in the orbit is $E = K + U = \dfrac{GMm}{2r} - \dfrac{GMm}{r} = -\dfrac{GMm}{2r} = -K$.

Given $K = 1.69 \times 10^{10} \text{ J}$, the total energy is $E = -1.69 \times 10^{10} \text{ J}$.

To escape into outer space, the final total energy of the satellite must be at least $0$.

The required additional energy $\Delta E$ is given by $E_{final} - E_{initial} = 0 - E = -(-K) = K$.

Therefore, the additional kinetic energy required is equal to the current kinetic energy, which is $1.69 \times 10^{10} \text{ J}$.

Answer: $1.69 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{ J}$

23320.subject: Physics
23320.text: A body is executing SHM. When its displacements from the mean position are $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $5 \mathrm{ cm}$ it has velocity $10 \mathrm{ cms}^{-1}$ and $8 \mathrm{ cms}^{-1}$ respectively. Its periodic time $\mathrm{t}$ is
23320.sol:
The velocity $v$ of a particle executing simple harmonic motion at a displacement $x$ is given by $v = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$, where $A$ is the amplitude and $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

For the first case, $10 = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - 4^2} \Rightarrow 100 = \omega^2 (A^2 - 16)$.

For the second case, $8 = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - 5^2} \Rightarrow 64 = \omega^2 (A^2 - 25)$.

Dividing the two equations: $\dfrac{100}{64} = \dfrac{A^2 - 16}{A^2 - 25} \Rightarrow \dfrac{25}{16} = \dfrac{A^2 - 16}{A^2 - 25}$.

Cross-multiplying: $25(A^2 - 25) = 16(A^2 - 16) \Rightarrow 25A^2 - 625 = 16A^2 - 256$.

$9A^2 = 369 \Rightarrow A^2 = 41$.

Substituting $A^2 = 41$ into the first equation: $100 = \omega^2 (41 - 16) = 25 \omega^2$.

$\omega^2 = 4 \Rightarrow \omega = 2 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

The periodic time $T$ is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi \text{ sec}$.

Answer: $\pi$ sec

23782.text: A particle is projected at an angle $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with horizontal having kinetic energy $K$. The kinetic energy of the particle at highest point is.
23782.sol:
Let the initial velocity of the particle be $u$. The initial kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^2$.

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of the velocity becomes zero, while the horizontal component remains constant. The horizontal component of the velocity is $v_x = u \cos \theta$, where $\theta = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The kinetic energy at the highest point $K'$ is given by $K' = \dfrac{1}{2}m(v_x)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m(u \cos 30^{{}^{\circ}})^2$.

Substituting $\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, we get $K' = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2$.

Since $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^2$, we have $K' = K \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}K$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4} K$

p V-p b & =n R T \\
\frac{p V}{n R T}$& =1+$\frac{p b}{n R T}\\

For any real number $x$, let $[x]$ denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $x$. Let $f$ be a real valued function defined on the interval $[-10,10]$ by $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}x-[x] & \text{ if }[x] \text{ is odd } \\ 1+[x]-x & \text{ if }[x] \text{ is even }\end{array}\right.$.

25433.sol: Given, $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}x-[x] & \text{ if }[x] \text{ is odd } \\ 1+[x]-x & \text{ if }[x] \text{is even }\end{array}$\right.f(x)$ and $\cos \pi x$ both are periodic with period 2 and both are even. $\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad$& \int_{-10}^{10} f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \\ & =2 \int_0^{10} f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \end{aligned} $$ \\ $\begin{aligned}$& =10 \int_0^2 f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \\ & \text{ Now, } \quad \int_$0^1 f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \\ & =\int_0^1(1-x) \cos $\pi$x d x=-\int_0^1 u \cos $\pi$u d u \\ & $\text{$ and $} \int_$1^2 f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \\ & =\int_1^2(x-1) \cos $\pi$x d x=-\int_0^1 u \cos $\pi$u d u \\ & \therefore \quad \int_{-10}^{10} f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x \\ & =-20 \int_0^1 u \cos $\pi$u d u=$\frac{40}{\pi^2}\\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\pi^2}{10}$ \int_{-10}^{10}$f(x) \cos $\pi$x d x=4 \end{aligned} $

26324.text: Two identical moving coil galvanometer have $10Ω$ resistance and full scale deflection at $2\muA$ current. One of them is converted into a voltmeter of $100mV$ full scale reading and the other into an Ammeter of $1mA$ full scale current using appropriate resistors. These are then used to measure the voltage and current in the Ohm's law experiment with $R = 1000Ω$ resistor by using an ideal cell. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
options: The resistance of the Voltmeter will be  $100kΩ .$
The measured value of  $R$  will be  $978Ω < R < 982Ω .$
The resistance of the Ammeter will be  $0.02Ω$  (round off to  ${2}^{nd}$  decimal place)
If the ideal cell is replaced by a cell having internal resistance of  $5Ω$  then the measured value of  $R$  will be more than  $1000Ω .$
26324.sol:
Voltmeter rom galvanometer arrangement.
Given: ${R}_{g} = 10Ω$ and ${I}_{g} = 2\muA$
Required voltage range, $V = 100 \times {10}^{- 3}volts$
$⇒ V = {I}_{g}\left({R}_{g} + {R}_{v}\right) = {10}^{- 1}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{10}^{- 1}}{2 \times {10}^{- 6}} = {R}_{g} + {R}_{v}\left(as, {I}_{g} = 2\muA\right)$
$⇒ 5 \times {10}^{4}Ω \approx {R}_{v} ( {R}_{v} < {10}^{5}Ω ) ⇒$ Option $( A )$ is incorrect.

Galvanometer to Ammeter arrangement
$\Delta{V}_{G} = \Delta{V}_{S}$
${I}_{g} ⋅ {R}_{g} = \left(I - {I}_{g}\right) ⋅ S$
$⇒ S = \dfrac{{I}_{g} ⋅ {R}_{g}}{I - {I}_{g}} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 10}{{10}^{- 3} - 2 \times {10}^{- 6}}$
$⇒ S = 2 \times {10}^{- 5} \times {10}^{3} = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$
$⇒ S = 20mΩ ⇒ ( C )$ is correct.
Circuit diagram for ohm's law

Resistance ammeter,
${R}_{A} = \dfrac{20 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10}{10} = 20 \times {10}^{- 3}Ω$
$i = \dfrac{ε}{\left(\dfrac{1000 \times 50 \times {10}^{3}}{51 \times {10}^{3}}\right)} = \dfrac{51ε}{5 \times {10}^{4}}\left(∵ {R}_{A} \to 0\right)$
${i}^{′} = i\left(\dfrac{{R}_{v}}{51 \times {10}^{3}}\right) = \dfrac{ε}{1000}$
Measured resistance $∴ {R}_{m} = \dfrac{{i}^{′} \times 1000}{i} = \dfrac{ε}{51ε} \times 5 \times {10}^{4} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{4}}{51} = 980.4Ω$
If the voltmeter shows full scale deflection then

$∴ ε = 999.6mv$

26499.text:
Paragraph: When a particle of mass $m$ moves on the $x$-axis in a potential of the form $V(x)=k x^2$, it performs simple harmonic motion.
The corresponding time period is proportional to $\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$, as can be seen easily using dimensional analysis. However, the motion of a particle can be periodic even when its potential energy increases on both sides of $x=0$ in a way different from $k x^2$ and its total energy is such that the particle does not escape to infinity. Consider a particle of mass $\mathrm{m}$ moving on the $x$-axis. Its potential energy is $V(x)=\alpha x^4(\alpha>0)$ for $|x|$ near the origin and becomes a constant equal to $V_0$ for $|x| \geq X_0$ (see figure).Question: The acceleration of this particle for $|x|>X_0$ is
options:
proportional to $V_0$

proportional to $\frac{V_0}{m X_0}$

proportional to $\sqrt{\frac{V_0}{m X_0}}$

Zero
26499.sol:
For $|x|>X_0$, potential energy is constant. Hence, kinetic energy, speed or velocity will also remain constant.
$\therefore$ Acceleration will be zero.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

26643.text: A human body has a surface area of approximately $1{m}^{2}$ . The normal body temperature is $10K$ above the surrounding room temperature ${T}_{0}$ . Take the room temperature to be ${T}_{0} = 300K$ . For ${T}_{0} = 300K$ , the value of $\sigma{T}^{4} = 460\dfrac{W}{{m}^{2}}$ (where $\sigma$ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant). Which of the following options is/are correct?
options: If the surrounding temperature reduces by a small amount ${ΔT}_{0} < < {T}_{0}$ , then to maintain the same body temperature the same (living) human being needs to radiate $ΔW = 4σ{T}_{0}^{3}{ΔT}_{0}$ more energy per unit time
Reducing the exposed surface area of the body (e.g. by curling up) allows humans to maintain the same body temperature while reducing the energy lost by radiation.
If the body temperature rises significantly then the peak in the spectrum of electromagnetic radiation emitted by the body would shift to longer wavelengths
The amount of energy radiated by the body in 1 second is close to $60Joules$
26643.sol:
$\begin{aligned}

& \text{ Energy radiated }=\sigma A\left(T^4-T_0^4\right) \mathrm{t} \\

& =\sigma A\left[\left(\mathrm{ T}_0+10\right)^4-T_0^4\right] t \\

& =\sigma A T_0^4\left[\left(1+\frac{10}{T_0}\right)^4-1\right] t \\

& =\sigma A T_0^4\left[\frac{40}{T_0}\right] \times t=460 \times 1 \times \frac{40}{300} \times 1=61.33 J \\

& P=\frac{\text{ Energy radiated }}{\text{ time }}=\sigma A T^4-\sigma A T_0^4 \\

& \therefore\left|\frac{d p}{d T_0}\right|=\sigma A\left(4 T_0^3\right) \therefore|d p|=\sigma A\left(4 T_0^3\right) d T_0 \\

& \therefore|\Delta P|=4 \sigma A T_0^3

\end{aligned}\)

A, B are not correct options as human body is not a black body. Energy radiated \(\propto \mathrm{A}\) where \(\mathrm{A}\) is$ the $surface area of the body. ' \(\mathrm{C}\) ' is the correct option$

29224.text: The correct order of spin-only magnetic moments among the following is: (Atomic number: $\mathrm{Mn}=$ $25, \mathrm{Co}=27, \mathrm{Ni}=28, \mathrm{Zn}=30$ )
29224.sol:
The complex having higher number of unpaired electrons will have higher value of spin only magnetic moment.
In all these complexes, the central metal ion is in $+2$ oxidation state.
$\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ has $3 d^{10}$ outer electronic configuration with 0 unpaired electron.
$\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ has $3 d^8$ outer electronic configuration with 2 unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ has $3 d^7$ outer electronic configuration with 3 unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ has $3 d^5$ outer electronic configuration with 5 unpaired electrons
Hence the correct order of spin-only magnetic moments is

$\left[\mathrm{MnCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}>\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_{4}$\right]^{2-}>$\left[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}>\left[\mathrm{ZnCl}_{4}$\right]^{2-} $\text{. }$

29318.text: Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12 . The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is ____. (Nearest integer).

Electrolysis of NaCl is
$\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{NaOH}(\mathrm{aq})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{ g})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{ g})$

Since during electrolysis pH changes to 12
So $\left[\mathrm{OH}^{\ominus}\right]=10^{-2} and \left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-12}$
So by Faraday law
Gram amount of substance deposited $=$ Amount of electricity passed


$\begin{aligned} & 10^{-2} \times \frac{600}{1000} \times 96500=\mathrm{I} \times \mathrm{t} \\ & \frac{10^{-2} \times 600}{1000} \times 96500=\mathrm{I} \times 5 \times 60 \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{10^{-2} \times 600 \times 96500}{1000 \times 5 \times 60} \\ & \mathrm{I}=1.93 \text{ ampere } \\ & \text{ So }, I=2 \text{ ampere (nearest integer) }\end{aligned}$

29843.sol:
(A) Chloroform $+$ Aniline $\to$ $III$ Distillation

(B) Benzoic acid $+$ Napthalene $\to IV$ Crystallisation

(C) Water $+$ Aniline $\to I$ Steam distillation

(D) Napthalene $+$ Sodium chloride $\to II$ Sublimation

Aniline is purified using the process of steam distillation because aniline is steam volatile and it is insoluble in water.

Chloroform and aniline having boiling points $334K$ and $457K$ can be separated by distillation. More volatile chloroform vaporizes first and is collected in the receiver. Aniline is left in the distillation flask.

Benzoic acid is soluble in hot water but naphthalene is not soluble, hence separation can be carried out by hot water crystallisation.

Naphthalene can also be separated by sublimation from non-volatile at room temperature.

The vapor of naphthalene can be collected and solidified.

30729.subject: Chemistry
30729.text: Given is a concentrated solution of a weak electrolyte $A_xB_y$ of concentration 'c' and dissociation constant 'K'. The degree of dissociation is given by :
30729.sol:
The dissociation reaction of the weak electrolyte $A_xB_y$ is:

$A_xB_y \rightleftharpoons xA^{y+} + yB^{x-}$

Initial concentrations:
$c \quad 0 \quad 0$

Equilibrium concentrations:
$c(1-\alpha) \quad cx\alpha \quad cy\alpha$

The dissociation constant $K$ is given by:

$K = \dfrac{[A^{y+}]^x [B^{x-}]^y}{[A_xB_y]}$

$K = \dfrac{(cx\alpha)^x (cy\alpha)^y}{c(1-\alpha)}$

$K = \dfrac{c^{x+y} x^x y^y \alpha^{x+y}}{c(1-\alpha)}$

$K = \dfrac{c^{x+y-1} x^x y^y \alpha^{x+y}}{1-\alpha}$

For a weak electrolyte, the degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is very small, so $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

$K = c^{x+y-1} x^x y^y \alpha^{x+y}$

Solving for $\alpha$:

$\alpha^{x+y} = \dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1} x^x y^y}$

$\alpha = \left(\dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1} x^x y^y}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{x+y}}$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1} x^x y^y}\right)^{\frac{1}{x+y}}$

32935.subject: Mathematics
32935.text: The minimum value of $\alpha$ for which the equation $\dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1}{1 - sinx} = \alpha$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is______.
32935.sol:
Let

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1}{1 - sinx}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1 + sinx}{1 - \sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 4cosecx + {sec}^{2}x + tanxsecx$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4cosx}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{2sinx + 1}{\cos^{3}x} + \dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4cosx}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2sinx\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(sinx + 1\right)\cos^{4}x + 3\cos^{2}xsinx{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{6}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2sinx\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(sinx + 1\right){\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}^{2} + 3\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)sinx{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}^{3}}$

For critical points,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{3}x} = \dfrac{4cosx}{\sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2} = 4\cos^{4}x$

$⇒ sinx\left(sinx + 1\right) = 2\cos^{2}x$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x + sinx = 2 - 2\sin^{2}x$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + sinx - 2 = 0$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + 3sinx - 2sinx - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3sinx - 2\right)\left(sinx + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ sinx = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Since, $sinx > 0 ∀ x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Now, at $sinx = \dfrac{2}{3}$, we get

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \dfrac{8}{27} - \dfrac{4}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}{\dfrac{16}{81}}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}{\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}^{2} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{25}{9}}{{\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}^{3}}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = \left[4\left[\dfrac{28}{27} \times \dfrac{81}{16}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}{\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)}^{2} + 3\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{25}{9}}{{\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)}^{3}}\right] > 0$

Hence, it is the point of minima.

$∴ f{\left(x\right)}_{min} = \dfrac{4}{\dfrac{2}{3}} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{2}{3}} = 9$

$f{\left(x\right)}_{max} \to \infty$

$f\left(x\right)$ is continuous function

$∴ {\alpha}_{min} = 9$

34127.subject: Mathematics
34127.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \dfrac{\log_e(x)}{x^2 + 4}\,dx$ is:
34127.sol:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_0^\infty \dfrac{\log_e(x)}{x^2 + 4}\,dx$

Substitute $x = 2 \tan \theta$, which gives $dx = 2 \sec^2 \theta \,d\theta$.

The limits of integration change from $x = 0 \to \theta = 0$ to $x \to \infty \to \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

$I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\log_e(2 \tan \theta)}{4 \tan^2 \theta + 4} (2 \sec^2 \theta) \,d\theta$

$I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\log_e(2 \tan \theta)}{4 \sec^2 \theta} (2 \sec^2 \theta) \,d\theta$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e(2 \tan \theta) \,d\theta$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} (\log_e 2 + \log_e(\tan \theta)) \,d\theta$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \log_e 2 \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} 1 \,d\theta + \dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e(\tan \theta) \,d\theta$

Let $I_1 = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e(\tan \theta) \,d\theta$

Using the property $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx = \displaystyle\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, we get:

$I_1 = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e\left(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)\right) \,d\theta = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e(\cot \theta) \,d\theta$

$I_1 = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e\left(\dfrac{1}{\tan \theta}\right) \,d\theta = -\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \log_e(\tan \theta) \,d\theta = -I_1$

$2I_1 = 0 \Rightarrow I_1 = 0$

Substituting $I_1 = 0$ back into the equation for $I$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \log_e 2 \left[\theta\right]_0^{\pi/2} + 0$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \log_e 2 \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi \log_e 2}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi\log_e(2)}{4}$

So, ${b}_{n} = {n}^{2}$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{15}{a}_{n} \cdot {b}_{n} = \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{15}\left(2{n}^{3} - {n}^{2}\right) = \mathop{2 ∑}_{n = 1}^{15}{n}^{3} - \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{15}{n}^{2}$

$= 2{\left(\dfrac{15 \cdot 16}{2}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{15 \cdot 16 \cdot 31}{6}$

$= 27560$

37890.text: If the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{3} = \dfrac{y+a}{5} = \dfrac{z+b+1}{7}$ and $\dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y-b}{4} = \dfrac{z-2a}{7}$ lies on $xy$-plane, then the value of $a + b$ is :
37890.sol:
Let the point of intersection be $(x, y, 0)$ since it lies on the $xy$-plane.

For the first line, equating the coordinates to a parameter $\lambda$:

$\dfrac{x+1}{3} = \dfrac{y+a}{5} = \dfrac{0+b+1}{7} = \lambda$

This gives $x = \dfrac{3b+3}{7} - 1$ and $y = \dfrac{5b+5}{7} - a$.

For the second line, equating the coordinates to a parameter $\mu$:

$\dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y-b}{4} = \dfrac{0-2a}{7} = \mu$

This gives $x = \dfrac{-2a}{7} + 2$ and $y = \dfrac{-8a}{7} + b$.

Equating the $x$-coordinates from both lines:

$\dfrac{3b+3}{7} - 1 = \dfrac{-2a}{7} + 2$

$\dfrac{3b-4}{7} = \dfrac{-2a+14}{7}$

$2a + 3b = 18$

Equating the $y$-coordinates from both lines:

$\dfrac{5b+5}{7} - a = \dfrac{-8a}{7} + b$

$5b + 5 - 7a = -8a + 7b$

$a - 2b = -5$

Solving the two linear equations $2a + 3b = 18$ and $a - 2b = -5$:

From the second equation, $a = 2b - 5$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$2(2b - 5) + 3b = 18$

$4b - 10 + 3b = 18$

$7b = 28 \Rightarrow b = 4$

Substituting $b = 4$ into $a = 2b - 5$:

$a = 2(4) - 5 = 3$

Therefore, $a + b = 3 + 4 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

The capacitive reactance of the circuit is given by, 

$\begin{cases}{X}_{c} & = & \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} \\ & = & \dfrac{\pi}{2\pi \times 50 \times {10}^{- 3}} \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$

The inductive reactance of the circuit is given by, 

$\begin{cases}{X}_{L} & = & \omegaL \\ & = & 2\pi \times 50 \times \dfrac{100}{\pi} \times {10}^{- 3} \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$

From above calculations, it is clear that

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$

$∴$ Power factor $= \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{R} = 1$

38894.text: In the figure shown, a circuit contains two identical resistors with resistance $R = 5Ω$ and an inductance with $L = 2mH .$ An ideal battery of $15V$ is connected in the circuit. What will be the current through the battery long after the switch is closed?
38894.sol:
After a long time, when the growth of current in the circuit has stopped, the inductor will work as a conductor. Therefore the effective resistance of the circuit will be,

$R = \dfrac{5}{2} = 2 . 5Ω$

Hence, the current through the circuit will be,

$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{15}{2.5} = 6A$

40181.text: A certain elastic conducting material is stretched into a circular loop. It is placed with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B = 0 . 8T$. When released the radius of the loop starts shrinking at a constant rate of $2cm{s}^{– 1}$. The induced emf in the loop at an instant when the radius of the loop is $10cm$ will be ______ $mV$.
40181.sol:
According to the Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the emf induced in a conducting loop is given by, $e = - \dfrac{d ϕ}{d t}$, here, $t$ is time and $ϕ = BA$ is magnetic flux.

Here, $e = \left|\dfrac{d ϕ}{d t}\right| = \dfrac{d \left(BA\right)}{d t} = B\dfrac{d \left(\pi{r}^{2}\right)}{d t}$

$= B\pi\left(2r\dfrac{d r}{d t}\right) = 2 \times \pi \times 0 . 1 \times 0 . 8 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$\approx 10mV$ (rounded off)

40567.text:
A $1m$ long copper wire carries a current of $1A$. If the cross section of the wire is $2 . 0{mm}^{2}$ and the resistivity of copper is $1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$. The force experienced by moving electron in the wire is _____$\times {10}^{- 23}N$

(Charge of electron$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$ )
40567.sol:
Given here, length $l = 1m$, current $i = 1A$, area $A = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}m$ and resistivity $ρ = 1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$.

Resistance of wire is $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 1}{2 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}Ω$

Now, electric field in the wire is $E = ρJ$, where, $J = \dfrac{i}{A}$ is current density.

Thus, $E = \dfrac{iρ}{A} = iR = 1 \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}V{m}^{- 1}$

Electric force in terms of electric field is given by $F = qE$

Therefore, force experienced by moving electron is $F = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 1 . 36 \times {10}^{- 21}$$= 136 \times {10}^{- 23}N$

40568.text: A long cylindrical volume contains a uniformly distributed charge of density $ρC{m}^{- 3}$. The electric field inside the cylindrical volume at a distance $x = \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}}{ρ}m$ from its axis is _____ $V{m}^{- 1}$.
40568.sol:
Given here, Volume charge density $= ρC{m}^{- 3}$.

Consider a Gaussian cylindrical surface of height $h$ and radius $x$.

Let $q$ charge is enclosed by the cylinder of radius $x$.

From Gauss's law,

$∫ E d Scos0 = \dfrac{q}{{ε}_{0}}$

Here, $q =$volume charge density$\times$volume of imaginary cylinder.

$⇒ E\left(2\pixh\right) = \dfrac{ρ \times \pi{x}^{2}h}{{ε}_{0}}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{ρx}{2{ε}_{0}}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{ρ}{2{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}}{ρ} = 1$

Thus, electric field is $1V{m}^{- 1}$.

At $t = 1s$, $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}$

The force is written as $\overset{\to}{F} = m\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}}{2} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

Comparing it with the given value of force, $x = 3$.

44468.subject: Physics
44468.text: A driver in a car, approaching a vertical wall notices that the frequency of his car horn has changed from $440Hz$ to $480Hz$, when it gets reflected from the wall. If the speed of sound in air is $345m{s}^{- 1}$, then the speed of the car is:
44468.sol:
Given,

Frequency of sound after reflection from the wall is

${f}^{' '} = 480Hz$

Frequency of sound emitted by the horn of car is

$f = 440Hz$

Speed of sound is $v = 345m{s}^{- 1}$

The diver in the car (as a source) approaching the vertical wall which is the observer in this case, The frequency of sound received by the stationary wall is given by

${f}_{r}^{'} = \left(\dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{c}}\right)f . . . ( 1 )$

As the frequency ${f}^{'}$ is received by wall will act as a source now, and driver in the car is an observer, the frequency of sound received by driver is ,

${f}_{r}^{' '} = \left(\dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v}\right){f}^{'} . . . ( 2 )$

Equating equation (1) and (2) we get,

${f}_{r}^{' '} = \left(\dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - {v}_{c}}\right)f . . . ( 3 )$

Substitute the given value in the equation (3), we get
$⇒ 480 = \left[\dfrac{345 + {v}_{c}}{345 - {v}_{c}}\right]440$

$⇒ \dfrac{12}{11} = \dfrac{345 + {v}_{c}}{345 - {v}_{c}}$

Velocity of car is given by

$⇒ {v}_{c} = 54km{hr}^{- 1}$

44698.text: A person trying to lose weight by burning fat lifts a mass of 10 kg upto a height of 1m 1000 times. Assume that the potential energy lost each time he lowers the mass is dissipated. How much fat will he use up considering the work done only when the weight is lifted up? Fat supplies $3.8 \times {10}^{7}$ J of energy per kg which is converted to mechanical energy with a 20% efficiency rate. Take $g = 9.8m{s}^{- 2}$ :
44698.sol:
$m = 10kg, h = 1m, 1000times$

Work done against gravity mgh

$= 10 \times 1 \times 9.8 = 98J$

In lifting 1000 times

$= 1000 \times 98$

$= 9.8 \times {10}^{4}J$

Fat burn with 20% efficiency $= 3.8 \times {10}^{7}J \times 0.2$

$= 7.6 \times {10}^{6}J$ per kg

$m = \dfrac{9.8 \times {10}^{4}}{7.6 \times {10}^{6}} = 1.289 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 12.89 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$

46103.text: Two rectangular blocks $A$ and $B$ of masses 2 kg and 3 kg respectively are connected by a spring of spring constant $10.8 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ and are placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. 46103.sol: As the block $A$ moves with velocity $0.15 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, it compresses the spring which pushes $B$ towards right. A goes on compressing the spring till the velocity acquired by $B$ becomes equal to the velocity of $A$, i.e., $0.15 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. Let this velocity be $v$. Now, spring is in a state of maximum compression. Let $x$ be the maximum compression at this stage. According to the law of conservation of linear momentum, we get $m_A u=\left(m_A+m_B\right) v$ or $v=\frac{m_A u}{m_A+m_B}$ $=\frac{2 \times 0.15}{2+3}=0.06 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ According to the law of conservation of energy. $\frac{1}{2} m_A u^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(m_A+m_B\right) v^2+\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ $\frac{1}{2} m_A u^2-\frac{1}{2}\left(m_A+m_B\right) v^2=\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times(0.15)^2-\frac{1}{2}(2+3)(0.06)^2=\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ $0.0225-0.009=\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ or $\quad 0.0135=\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ or $\quad x=\sqrt{\frac{0.027}{k}}=\sqrt{\frac{0.027}{10.8}}=0.05 \mathrm{~m}$

56844.subject: Chemistry
56844.text: Which among the following is common for electrolysis of molten NaCl and aqueous NaCl ?
56844.sol:
Electrolysis of molten and aqueous NaCl share only one common product: chlorine gas evolved at the anode.

For molten NaCl, the only ions present are Na^+$ and Cl^-$. Reduction of Na^+$ occurs at the cathode: Na^+$ + e^-$ → Na_{(s)}. Oxidation of Cl^-$ occurs at the anode: 2Cl^-$ → Cl_{2(g)} + 2e^-$.

For aqueous NaCl, the system contains Na^+$, Cl^-$, H^+$, and OH^-$. At the cathode, water is reduced instead of sodium due to its higher reduction potential: 2H_{2}O + 2e^-$ → H_{2(g)} + 2OH^-$. At the anode, chlorine is oxidized despite water’s lower oxidation potential, due to overpotential and high chloride concentration: 2Cl^-$ → Cl_{2(g)} + 2e^-$.

Both processes liberate Cl_{2} gas at the anode, making it the common product. Sodium metal and hydrogen gas are cathode products exclusive to molten and aqueous electrolysis respectively, while NaOH formation is unique to the aqueous case.

57625.text: Which among the following is an allylic halide?

An allylic halide contains a halogen attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

Examining the options:

A) 1-Bromopropene (CH_3-CH=CH-Br$): bromine is attached to an $sp^2$ carbon, making this vinylic.

B) 2-Bromopropene (CH_2=C(Br)CH_3$): bromine is attached to an $sp^2$ carbon, also vinylic.

C) 3-Bromopropene (CH_2=CH-CH_2Br$): bromine is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the double bond, satisfying the allylic condition.

D) 4-Bromobut-1-ene (BrCH_2CH_2CH=CH_2$): bromine is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon, but it is not adjacent to the double bond, so it is homoallylic.

The allylic halide is $\boxed{C}$.

60253.subject: Mathematics
60253.text: The rate of change of volume of spherical balloon at any instant is directly proportional to its surface area. If initially its radius is 3 cm , after 2 minutes its radius becomes 9 cm , then radius of balloon after 4 minutes is
60253.sol:
A spherical balloon's volume and surface area are expressed by $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and $A = 4\pi r^2$, respectively, for radius $r$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt} = kA$ with proportionality constant $k$, differentiate $V$:

$\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \frac{dr}{dt}$

Substituting into the proportional relation:

$4\pi r^2 \frac{dr}{dt} = k(4\pi r^2)$

Simplify by dividing through by $4\pi r^2$ (for $r \neq 0$):

$\frac{dr}{dt} = k$

This indicates a constant rate of change of the radius. Integrate with respect to $t$:

$r(t) = kt + C$

Given $r(0) = 3$, we find $C = 3$, so $r(t) = kt + 3$; with $r(2) = 9$, solve $9 = 2k + 3$ yielding $k = 3$, hence $r(t) = 3t + 3$. Evaluate at $t = 4$:

$r(4) = 3(4) + 3 = 15$

Final answer: $\boxed{15}$ cm

61672.subject: Mathematics
61672.text: If $y = x + e^x$, then $\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2}$ is equal to
61672.sol:
Given $y = x + e^x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + e^x$

Taking the reciprocal:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x}$

Differentiating with respect to $y$:

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{d}{dy} \left( \dfrac{dx}{dy} \right) = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{dx}{dy} \right) \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dy}$

Substituting the values:

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} \right) \cdot \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} \right)$

62704.text: If $\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c}{x^2 - 2x + 1} = 2026$ then the value of $a - c$ is...
62704.sol:
Let $f(x) = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c$.

For the limit to exist and be finite, the denominator $(x-1)^2$ must be a factor of the numerator $f(x)$.

Let $f(x) = (x-1)^2(x-k)$.

Expanding this, we get $f(x) = (x^2-2x+1)(x-k) = x^3 - (k+2)x^2 + (2k+1)x - k$.

Comparing the coefficients, we have $a = -(k+2)$ and $c = -k$.

The limit is given by $\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{(x-1)^2(x-k)}{(x-1)^2} = \lim_{x \to 1} (x-k) = 1-k$.

Given that the limit is $2026$, we have $1-k = 2026 \Rightarrow k = -2025$.

We need to find the value of $a-c$.

$a-c = -(k+2) - (-k) = -k - 2 + k = -2$.

Answer: $-2$

65580.subject: Physics
65580.text: A light bulb connected in series with a capacitor and an a.c.source is glowing with certain brightness. On reducing the value of capacitance and frequency respectively, the brightness of the bulb
65580.sol:
The brightness of the bulb depends on the current flowing through it, which is given by $I = \dfrac{V}{Z}$.

The impedance of the series RC circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}$, where $X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$.

When the capacitance $C$ is reduced, the capacitive reactance $X_C$ increases. This increases the total impedance $Z$ of the circuit, which in turn reduces the current $I$. Consequently, the brightness of the bulb is reduced.

Similarly, when the frequency $f$ of the AC source is reduced, the capacitive reactance $X_C$ increases. This again increases the impedance $Z$ and reduces the current $I$. Thus, the brightness of the bulb is reduced.

Therefore, in both cases, the brightness of the bulb is reduced.

Answer: is reduced, is reduced

66077.subject: Physics
66077.text: A parallel plate air capacitor has capacitance $C_p$. It is equally filled with parallel layers of materials of dielectric constants $\mathrm{K}_1$ and $\mathrm{K}_2$. Now its capacity becomes $C_K$. The ratio $C_P$ to $C_K$ is
66077.sol:
Capacitance of parallel plate air capacitor
The capacitance of an air capacitor with plate area $A$ and plate separation $d$ is $C_p = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

Capacitance with dielectric layers
When filled with two dielectric layers of equal thickness $d/2$ and dielectric constants $K_1$ and $K_2$, the configuration forms two capacitors in series. The individual capacitances are $C_1 = \frac{2K_1\epsilon_0 A}{d}$ and $C_2 = \frac{2K_2\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

The equivalent capacitance satisfies $\frac{1}{C_K} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} = \frac{d}{2\epsilon_0 A}\left(\frac{1}{K_1} + \frac{1}{K_2}\right)$, yielding $C_K = \frac{2\epsilon_0 A}{d}\left(\frac{K_1 K_2}{K_1 + K_2}\right)$.

Ratio calculation
The ratio becomes $\frac{C_p}{C_K} = \frac{\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}}{\frac{2\epsilon_0 A}{d}\left(\frac{K_1 K_2}{K_1 + K_2}\right)} = \frac{K_1 + K_2}{2K_1 K_2}$.

This corresponds to option C.

66805.subject: Physics
66805.text: A copper ring is held horizontally and a bar magnet is dropped through the ring with its length along the axis of the ring. The acceleration of the falling magnet while it is passing through the ring is
options: more than acceleration due to gravity.
less than acceleration due to gravity.
depends on the diameter of ring and length of magnet.
depends on pole strength of magnet.
66805.sol:
The falling magnet induces a current in the copper ring due to changing magnetic flux. According to Lenz's Law, the induced current always opposes the motion causing it, creating an upward electromagnetic force that counteracts gravity.

This results in a net downward force $F_{\text{net}} = mg - F_{\text{em}}$, where $F_{\text{em}} > 0$. Since acceleration $a = F_{\text{net}}/m$, we have $a < g$.

The magnet therefore falls with acceleration less than $g$.

67059.subject: Physics
67059.text: Two charges $\mathrm{q}_1=+6 \mathrm{q}$ and $\mathrm{q}_2=-3 \mathrm{q}$ are placed as shown in figure. A proton is placed on x -axis away from $\mathrm{q}_2$. To remain proton in equilibrium, the distance between $\mathrm{q}_1$ and proton is
67059.sol:
Equilibrium requires zero net electrostatic force on the proton. With charges $q_1 = +6q$ at $x=0$ and $q_2 = -3q$ at $x=L$, the equilibrium position must lie to the right of $q_2$ ($x > L$) since $|q_2| < |q_1|$ and both forces would otherwise act in the same direction.

Considering a proton at position $x > L$, the repulsive force from $q_1$ is $F_1 = k\frac{6qe}{x^2}$ and the attractive force from $q_2$ is $F_2 = k\frac{3qe}{(x-L)^2}$.

Setting $F_1 = F_2$ and canceling common factors $k$, $q$, and $e$:

$\frac{6}{x^2} = \frac{3}{(x-L)^2}$

Simplifying yields $\frac{2}{x^2} = \frac{1}{(x-L)^2}$.

Taking square roots (positive since $x > L$):

$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{x} = \frac{1}{x-L}$

Solving for $x$:

$\sqrt{2}(x-L) = x$

$x(\sqrt{2}-1) = \sqrt{2}L$

$x = \frac{\sqrt{2}L}{\sqrt{2}-1}$

The equilibrium position is $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}L}{\sqrt{2}-1}}$ to the right of the origin.

Similarly, magnetic field due to section EF is:

Total magnetic field at $\mathrm{O}$ is:
$\mathrm{B}=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{I}}{8}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}\right)$ inside the plane of paper.

70842.subject: Physics
70842.text: A constant force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ newton has a displacement $\vec{r}=2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k}$ metre in 2 second. The work done and the power are respectively
70842.sol:
The work done by a constant force is computed using the dot product of force and displacement vectors. Given $\overrightarrow{F} = 3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j} - \hat{k}\, \text{N}$ and $\overrightarrow{r} = 2 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j} - 3 \hat{k}\, \text{m}$, the work is $\overrightarrow{F} \cdot \overrightarrow{r} = (3)(2) + (-2)(-3) + (-1)(-3) = 6 + 6 + 3 = 15\, \text{J}$.

Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as $P = \frac{W}{t}$. With $W = 15\, \text{J}$ and $t = 2\, \text{s}$, power is $\frac{15}{2} = 7.5\, \text{W}$.

Option B corresponds to these values.

71392.subject: Biology
71392.text: In mutation breeding, which of the following does NOT represent chemical mutagens?
71392.sol:
Mutation breeding involves inducing mutations to develop new plant varieties with desirable traits. This can be achieved using physical or chemical mutagens.

Chemical mutagens include alkylating agents like methyl methane sulphonate (MMS), base analogues, and other compounds like sodium azide and hydroxylamine that alter DNA structure.

Colchicine is an alkaloid used primarily to induce polyploidy by inhibiting spindle fiber formation during cell division. While it causes genetic changes (changes in chromosome number), it is generally classified as a polyploidizing agent rather than a typical chemical mutagen that induces point mutations or structural chromosomal aberrations.

Therefore, in the context of typical chemical mutagens used for generating variations in breeding, colchicine is not considered one.

Answer: Colchicine

71512.subject: Biology
71512.text: Which one of the following plants shows helobial type endosperm?
71512.sol:
Endosperm development is of three main types: nuclear, cellular, and helobial.

Helobial endosperm is an intermediate type between nuclear and cellular endosperms. In this type, the first division of the primary endosperm nucleus is followed by the formation of a transverse wall, resulting in two unequal cells: a large micropylar cell and a small chalazal cell. Subsequent divisions in both cells are free nuclear. This type of endosperm is mostly found in monocotyledons, particularly in the order Helobiales.

Asphodelus is a classic example of a plant that exhibits the helobial type of endosperm.

Coconut shows both nuclear (coconut water) and cellular (white kernel) endosperm.

Balsam and Adoxa show cellular endosperm.

Answer: Asphodelus

71694.subject: Chemistry
71694.text: Which of the following molecules shows $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridisation?
71694.sol:
The hybridisation of a central atom can be determined using the formula for steric number ($H$):

$H = \dfrac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)$

where $V$ is the number of valence electrons on the central atom, $M$ is the number of monovalent atoms attached, $C$ is the cationic charge, and $A$ is the anionic charge.

For $\text{PCl}_5$:
Central atom is P ($V = 5$).
Number of monovalent Cl atoms ($M = 5$).
$H = \dfrac{1}{2}(5 + 5) = 5$
A steric number of $5$ corresponds to $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridisation.

For $\text{SO}_2$:
Central atom is S ($V = 6$).
Number of monovalent atoms ($M = 0$).
$H = \dfrac{1}{2}(6 + 0) = 3$ ($\text{sp}^2$ hybridisation).

For $\text{BF}_3$:
Central atom is B ($V = 3$).
Number of monovalent F atoms ($M = 3$).
$H = \dfrac{1}{2}(3 + 3) = 3$ ($\text{sp}^2$ hybridisation).

For $\text{CO}_2$:
Central atom is C ($V = 4$).
Number of monovalent atoms ($M = 0$).
$H = \dfrac{1}{2}(4 + 0) = 2$ ($\text{sp}$ hybridisation).

Thus, $\text{PCl}_5$ shows $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridisation.

Answer: $\text{PCl}_5$

71802.subject: Chemistry
71802.text: What type of isomerism is found in but-2-ene?
71802.sol:
But-2-ene has the chemical structure $CH_{3}-CH=CH-CH_{3}$.

Each carbon atom of the double bond is attached to two different groups, specifically a hydrogen atom and a methyl group.

Due to the restricted rotation around the carbon-carbon double bond, it can exist in two different spatial arrangements.

These arrangements correspond to the cis and trans isomers.

Thus, but-2-ene exhibits geometrical isomerism.

Answer: Geometrical isomerism

71836.subject: Chemistry
71836.text: What is the main product obtained when sodium ethoxide reacts with isopropyl chloride?
71836.sol:
Sodium ethoxide ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+$) acts as both a strong base and a strong nucleophile.

Isopropyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CHCl-CH}_3$) is a secondary alkyl halide.

When a secondary alkyl halide reacts with a strong base like sodium ethoxide, elimination (E2) competes with substitution (S_N$2). Due to the steric hindrance of the secondary alkyl halide and the strength of the base, dehydrohalogenation (elimination) dominates over substitution. \\ \\ Thus, the major product is an alkene (propene), while the substitution product (ethyl isopropyl ether) is formed only as a minor product. \\ \\ Reaction: \\ \text{CH}_3\text{-CHCl-CH}_3 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH}_2 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{Cl}^- \\ \\ Answer: \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH}_2$

Match List I with List II

(B). Covalent Solid(II). $K_2SO_4$

71947.sol:
Ionic solids are formed by the electrostatic attraction between cations and anions. $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$ is an ionic solid composed of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions.

Covalent or network solids consist of atoms held together by a continuous network of covalent bonds. Quartz ($\text{SiO}_2$) is a classic example of a covalent solid.

Molecular solids are composed of discrete molecules held together by intermolecular forces. Solid $\text{CO}_2$ (dry ice) is a molecular solid held together by London dispersion forces.

Metallic solids consist of a lattice of positive metal ions in a sea of delocalized electrons. Potassium ($\text{K}$) is a metallic solid.

Thus, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (III)

71981.subject: Chemistry
71981.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the ideal solution?
options: It obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration.
There is no heat evolved or absorbed when two components forming an ideal solution are mixed.
There is no volume change when two components forming an ideal solution are mixed.
The vapor pressure of the ideal solution can be higher or lower than those of pure components
71981.sol:
For an ideal solution, the following conditions hold true:

1. It obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration.

2. The enthalpy of mixing is zero, i.e., $\Delta H_{mix} = 0$. No heat is evolved or absorbed.

3. The volume of mixing is zero, i.e., $\Delta V_{mix} = 0$.

4. The total vapor pressure of the solution is given by $P_{total} = P_A^{0} x_{A} + P_B^{0} x_{B}$. Since $x_{A} + x_{B} = 1$, the total vapor pressure is a weighted average of the vapor pressures of the pure components. Therefore, the vapor pressure of an ideal solution always lies between the vapor pressures of the pure components. It cannot be higher or lower than both.

Thus, the statement that the vapor pressure of the ideal solution can be higher or lower than those of pure components is incorrect.

Answer: The vapor pressure of the ideal solution can be higher or lower than those of pure components

72075.subject: Physics
72075.text: If a coil of inductance L and resistance R is connected to AC source with voltage V and angular frequency $\omega$ and current I, then the inductance L is
72075.sol:
The impedance $Z$ of a coil having inductance $L$ and resistance $R$ in an AC circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$, where the inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L$.

From Ohm's law for AC circuits, the impedance is also given by $Z = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}$.

Equating the two expressions for impedance:

$\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}$

Squaring both sides:

$R^2 + \omega^2 L^2 = \left(\dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}\right)^2$

Rearranging to solve for $\omega^2 L^2$:

$\omega^2 L^2 = \left(\dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}\right)^2 - R^2$

Taking the square root of both sides:

$\omega L = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}\right)^2 - R^2}$

$L = \dfrac{1}{\omega} \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}\right)^2 - R^2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\omega} \left(\sqrt{ \left(\dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}}\right)^2-$ R^2}\right)

72331.subject: Physics
72331.text: When a particle in linear S.H.M. completes two oscillations, its phase changes by
72331.sol:
The phase of a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by $\phi = \omega t + \phi_0$.

The time period of one complete oscillation is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.

For two complete oscillations, the time elapsed is $\Delta t = 2T = \dfrac{4\pi}{\omega}$.

The change in phase is $\Delta \phi = \omega \Delta t = \omega \left(\dfrac{4\pi}{\omega}\right) = 4\pi$ radians.

Answer: $4\pi$ radian

72511.subject: Physics
72511.text: If two waves $y_1 = A\sin(\omega t - 0.1x)$ and $y_2 = A\sin  \left(\omegat -$0.1x - $\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$are superimposed on each other, then the resultant amplitude due to superposition of waves is
72511.sol:
The given waves are $y_1 = A\sin(\omega t - 0.1x)$ and $y_2 = A\sin \left(\omega$t - 0.1x - $\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right).

The phase difference between$ the $two waves is \Delta\phi = \dfrac{\phi}{2}.

The resultant amplitude$A_R$ of two superimposed waves is given by:

$A_R = $\sqrt{A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2A_1A_2\cos(\Delta\phi)}

Substituting $A_1 = A$, $A_2 = A, and $\Delta\phi = \dfrac{\phi}{2}:

$A_R = $\sqrt{A^2 + A^2 + 2A^2\cos\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)}

$A_R = $\sqrt{2A^2\left(1 + \cos\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)}

Using$ the trigonometric identity1 + \cos$\theta =$2\cos^2 $\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$:

$A_R = \sqrt{2A^2\left(2\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{4}\right)}$

$A_R = \sqrt{4A^2\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{4}}$

$A_R = 2A\cos\dfrac{\phi}{4}$

Answer: $2A\cos\dfrac{\phi}{4}$

77155.subject: Mathematics
77155.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $(x+y)^{p+q} = x^p y^q$, where $p$, $q$ are positive integers.

The derivative of $y$ with respect to $x$
77155.sol:
Given $(x+y)^{p+q} = x^p y^q$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$(p+q) \ln(x+y) = p \ln x + q \ln y$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \left(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{p}{x} + \dfrac{q}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:

$\dfrac{p+q}{x+y} - \dfrac{p}{x} = \left( \dfrac{q}{y} - \dfrac{p+q}{x+y} \right) \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Simplifying the left side:

$\dfrac{x(p+q) - p(x+y)}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{px + qx - px - py}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{x(x+y)}$

Simplifying the right side:

$\dfrac{q(x+y) - y(p+q)}{y(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx + qy - py - qy}{y(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{y(x+y)}$

Equating the two sides:

$\dfrac{qx - py}{x(x+y)} = \dfrac{qx - py}{y(x+y)} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Canceling the common terms from both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}$

The derivative $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is $\dfrac{y}{x}$, which is independent of both $p$ and $q$.

Answer: is independent of both $p$ and $q$

78241.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $3 x^2+2 x+1=0$, then the equation whose roots are $\alpha+\beta^{-1}$ and $\beta+\alpha^{-1}$ is
78241.sol:
$3 x^2+2 x+1=0$
Sum of the roots $=\alpha+\beta=\frac{-2}{3}$\ldots(1)
Product$ of the roots=\alpha \cdot \beta=\frac{1}{3}$\ldots(2)
We have$ to find the equation with the roots\alpha+\beta^{-1} and \beta+\alpha^{-1}$.
Sum of the roots $(S)=\alpha+\beta^{-1}+\beta+\alpha^{-1}=\alpha+\frac{1}{\beta}+\beta+\frac{1}{\alpha}\begin{aligned} & =(\alpha+\beta)+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha \beta}\right) \\ & =\frac{-2}{3}+\left(\frac{\frac{-2}{3}}{\frac{1}{3}}\right) \quad(\text{$ from $(1),(2)) }\end{aligned}=\frac{-2}{3}-2=\frac{-2-6}{3}=\frac{-8}{3} .$
Product of the roots $(\mathrm{P})=\left(\alpha+\beta^{-1}\right)\left(\beta+\alpha^{-1}\right)=\left(\alpha+\frac{1}{\beta}\right)\left(\beta+\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)=\alpha \beta+1+1+\frac{1}{\alpha \beta}=\alpha \beta+2+\frac{1}{\alpha \beta}=\frac{1}{3}+2+\frac{1}{\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{1}{3}+2+3=\frac{1}{3}+5=\frac{16}{3}$.
So, the required equation is $x^2-S . x .+P=0=x^2+\frac{8}{3} x+\frac{16}{3}=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2+8 x+16=0$

78517.subject: Mathematics
78517.text:
Consider the following for the four (04) items that follow:
The frequency distribution of height of students of a class is given below:
Height (in cm)Number of Students
160–16212
162–16415
164–16624
166–16813

What is the median height of the class?
78517.sol:
The cumulative frequencies for the given classes are:

$160-162$: $12$
$162-164$: $12 + 15 = 27$
$164-166$: $27 + 24 = 51$
$166-168$: $51 + 13 = 64$

Total number of students, $N = 64$
$\dfrac{N}{2} = \dfrac{64}{2} = 32$

The cumulative frequency just greater than $32$ is $51$, which corresponds to the class $164-166$. Thus, the median class is $164-166$.

Lower limit of the median class, $L = 164$
Cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class, $cf = 27$
Frequency of the median class, $f = 24$
Class width, $h = 2$

Using the formula for median:
$\text{Median} = L + \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{N}{2} - cf}{f} \right) \times h$

$\text{Median} = 164 + \left( \dfrac{32 - 27}{24} \right) \times 2$

$\text{Median} = 164 + \left( \dfrac{5}{24} \right) \times 2$

$\text{Median} = 164 + \dfrac{5}{12}$

$\text{Median} \approx 164 + 0.416 = 164.41 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $164.41$ cm

78935.text:
Consider the equation: $k \sin x+\cos 2 x=2 k-7$
If the equation possesses solution, then what is the minimum value of k ?
78935.sol:
$K \sin x+\cos 2 x=2 K-7K \sin x+\left(1-2 \sin ^2 x\right)=(2 K-7)2 \sin ^2 x-K \sin x+(2 K-8)=0$
This is a quadratic equation in $\sin x$.
$\sin x=\frac{-(-K) \pm \sqrt{K^2-4(2)(2 K-8)}}{2 \times 2}$
For minimum value of $K$, $\sin x=-1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{K \pm \sqrt{K^2-16 K+64}}{4}=-1 \\
& \Rightarrow( \pm) \sqrt{K^2-16 K+64}=-K-4
\end{aligned}$
Squaring both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& K^2-16 K+64=K^2+16+8 K \\
& \Rightarrow 24 K=48 \\
& \Rightarrow K=2
\end{aligned}$

79653.subject: Botany
79653.text: What is common about Trypanosoma. Noctiluca, Monocystis and Giardia?
79653.sol: Trypanosoma gambiense is the single celled, parasitic zoofiagellate causing trypanosomiasis or sleeping sickness. Giardia is a parasitic flagellate occurring in the intestine of man and other animals and causes giardiasis or diarrhoea (i.e., very loose and frequent stool containing large quantity of fat). Noctiluca is a marine, colourless dinoflagellate. It is a voracious predator and has a long, motile tentacle, near the base of which, its single short flagellum emerges. Monocystis is a microscopic, unicellular endoparasitic protozoan found in the coelom and seminal vesicles of earthworm. As it is an endoparasite, it does not possess any special structure for locomotion.

84059.subject: Zoology
84059.text: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents:
84059.sol:
An electrocardiogram (ECG), is a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle. The machine used to obtain an electrocardiogram is known as electrocardiography and this technique is called electrocardiography. The interpretation of ECG is as follows:

• The P wave is a small upward wave that represents electrical excitation (or depolarization) of the atria which leads to contraction of both the atria.
• The QRS (wave) complex represents the depolarization of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction (ventricular systole). The contraction of the ventricles start shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole.
• The T wave represents the return of the ventricles from excited (depolarized) to a normal state (i.e., repolarisation). The end of the T wave marks the end of the systole.
• Thus, by counting the number of QRS complexes that occur in a given time period, the heartbeat rate of an individual can be determined.

85000.subject: Zoology
85000.text: During transcription holoenzyme RNA polymerase binds to a DNA sequence and the DNA assumes a saddle like structure at that point. What is chat sequence called?
85000.sol:
A TATA box is a DNA sequence that indicates where a genetic sequence can be read and decoded. Promoter region is the proximal area of transcription unit, which provides site for attachment of transcription factors ( $\sigma$ factor) and RNA polymerase. It is present upstream at 5 ' end of coding strand. It has special structure; an AT rich area called TATA box or Pribnow box. The TATA box is able to define the direction of transcription and also indicates the DNA strand to be read.
Related Theory
The TATA box is named for its conserved DNA sequence, which is most commonly TATAAA. Many eukaryotic genes have a conserved TATA box located 25-35 base pairs before the transcription start site of a gene.

$\mathop{{\text{CH}_{3} - \overset{\text{OH}}{\overset{|}{C} =} \text{CH} - \overset{O}{\overset{| |}{C}} - {\text{CH}_{3}}_{\text{III}} > \mathop{{\text{CH}_{3} - \text{CO} - {\text{CH}_{2} - \text{CO} - {\text{CH}_{3}}_{\text{II}} > \mathop{{\text{CH}_{2} = \text{C}( \text{OH} ) - {\text{CH}_{2} - \text{CO} - {\text{CH}_{3}}_{I}$

I is less stable as (=) bond is not in conjugation with carbonly group.

III is most stable due to conjugation of (=) bond and intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

90830.text: If $f: R \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{e^{2x} - e^{- 2x}}{2},$ then
90830.sol:
Let us check for invertibility of $f\left(x\right)$
$\left(A\right)$ one-one: we have, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{2x} - {e}^{- 2x}}{2}$
$⇒ {f}^{′} \left(x\right) = \dfrac{{e}^{4x} + 1}{{e}^{2x}} ,$ which is strictly increasing as ${e}^{4x} > 0$ for all $x .$
Thus, $f$ is one-one
$\left(B\right)$ Onto: Let $y = f\left(x\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = {e}^{2x} + {e}^{- 2x},$ where y is strictly monotonic
Hence, the range of $f\left(x\right) = \left(f\left(- \infty\right), f\left(\infty\right)\right)$
$⇒$ range of $f\left(x\right) = \left(- \infty, \infty\right)$
So, the range of $f\left(x\right) =$ co-domain
Hence, $f\left(x\right)$ is one-one and onto
$\left(C\right)$ To find ${f}^{- 1}: y = \dfrac{{e}^{4x} - 1}{2{e}^{2x}}$
$⇒ {e}^{4x} - 2{e}^{2x}y - 1 = 0$
$⇒ {e}^{2x} = \dfrac{2y \pm \sqrt{4{y}^{2} + 4}}{2}$
$⇒ 2x = log\left(y \pm \sqrt{{y}^{2} + 1}\right)$
$⇒ {f}^{- 1}\left(y\right) = \dfrac{log\left(y \pm \sqrt{{y}^{2} + 1}\right)}{2}$
Since, ${e}^{{f}^{- 1}\left(x\right)}$ is always positive, so neglecting negative sign.
Hence, ${f}^{- 1}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{log\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)}{2}$

92613.text: A block $A$ of mass $m$ is in equilibrium after being suspended from the ceiling with the help of a spring of force constant $k$. The block $B$ of mass $m$, strikes the block $A$ with a speed $v$ and sticks to it. The value of $v$& for which the spring& just attains its natural length is
92613.sol:
Let the velocity of the combined system just after the collision is& $v '$, then using conservation of linear momentum we get

$mv = 2mv′$,

$⇒ v′ = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Initial elongation of the spring is

$x = \dfrac{mg}{k}$

Now, using the conservation of mechanical energy we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}2m\left(v '\right)2 + \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = 2mgx$

$m\left(\dfrac{v^{2}}{4}\right) + \dfrac{m^{2}g^{2}}{2k} = \dfrac{2m^{2}g^{2}}{k}$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{6mg^{2}}{k}}$

94168.sol:
The monochromatic ray of light will retrace its path if it strikes the mirror perpendicularly.

Using Snell's law of refraction,

$⇒ sin\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} \times sin45 °$

$sin\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = 60 °$

95980.sol: The cytoskeleton is a system of proteinaceous fibrillar structures that pervades the cytoplasm. 97750.subject: Botany
97750.text:
Select the CORRECT statements

(i) Between temperature range $0 – {25}^{o}C$, rate of respiration doubles for every ${10}^{o}C$ rise in temperature.
(ii) Cytochromes are iron-porphyrin compounds.
(iii) Respiratory rate of wounded or injured plant parts generally decreases.
97750.sol:
Respiration is part of the metabolic process where the nutrients are converted into useful energy for regular cell activities. It is in two mode depending on presence or absence of oxygen. Aerobic respiration is the one where oxygen is involved and anaerobic respiration is the process where oxygen is absent. One of the factor regulating rate of respiration is the temperature and the ${Q}_{10}$ temperature co-efficient for respiration in the range of $0 – {25}^{o}C$ is 2, which means rate of respiration doubles for every ${10}^{o}C$ rise in temperature. The rate of change of a biological or chemical system as a consequence of increasing the temperature by ${10}^{o}C$ is referred to as ${Q}_{10}$ temperature co-efficient which is a value without a unit.

Cytochromes are group of heme proteins and pigment molecules that undergo redox reactions aiding in ATP production in ETC. These are macromolecules made of porphyrin compounds having iron-component.

Respiratory rate of wounded or injured plant parts generally increases as it requires energy for healing and repair.

97891.subject: Botany
97891.text: If two organisms can't interbreed to produce fertile offsprings, you can't place them under a
97891.sol: The classification of all living organisms has been done by dividing them into different levels based on their features and characteristics. There is a hierarchy in this classification and each step represents a rank or category known as a taxonomic category. There are around seven main taxonomic ranks or categories - species, genus, family, order, class, phylum/division, and kingdom. Groups of individuals having similar fundamental qualities are called species. Species contain a group of interacting and interbreeding organisms. When the group of related species has more common characters among them they are referred to as genus. Families that exhibit few similar characters are placed under the same Order. All the fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the taxonomic level phylum.

100088.subject: Physics
100088.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Magnetic field(I) $[M^{-1}L^{-3}T^4A^2]$
(B) Magnetic flux(II) $[MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]$
(C) Magnetic permeability(III) $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$
(D) Electric permittivity(IV) $[MT^{-2}A^{-1}]$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
100088.sol:
To find the dimensional formulas, we use standard relations:

(A) Magnetic field ($B$): From the magnetic force $F = qvB$, we have $[B] = \dfrac{[F]}{[q][v]} = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}]}{[AT][LT^{-1}]} = [MT^{-2}A^{-1}]$. Thus, A matches with IV.

(B) Magnetic flux ($\Phi$): From $\Phi = BA$, we have $[\Phi] = [MT^{-2}A^{-1}][L^2] = [ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$. Thus, B matches with III.

(C) Magnetic permeability ($\mu_0$): From the force per unit length between parallel wires $\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi r}$, we have $[\mu_0] = \dfrac{[F][r]}{[L][I^2]} = \dfrac{[MLT^{-2}][L]}{[L][A^2]} = [MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]$. Thus, C matches with II.

(D) Electric permittivity ($\varepsilon_0$): From Coulomb's law $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$, we have $[\varepsilon_0] = \dfrac{[q^2]}{[F][r^2]} = \dfrac{[A^2T^2]}{[MLT^{-2}][L^2]} = [M^{-1}L^{-3}T^4A^2]$. Thus, D matches with I.

The correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

101075.subject: Physics
101075.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
101075.text: A neutron makes a head-on elastic collision with a stationary deuteron. The fractional energy loss of the neutron in the collision is
101075.sol: One deuteron consists of one proton and one neutron. As the mass of a proton and a neutron is approximately same $\left(\approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}\right)$, we assume that the mass of the neutron be $m$ and the mass of the deuteron be $2 m$ as the electron mass is negligibly small compared to that of proton and neutron. Let the initial velocity of the neutron be $u$. As the deuteron is initially at rest, the final velocity of the neutron is v_1=$\left(\frac{m-2 m}{m+2 m}\right)$u=-$\frac{m u}{3 m}=-\frac{u}{3} .$and the velocity of the deuteron is v_2=$\frac{2 m}{m+2 m}$u=$\frac{2}{3}$u $\text{. }$Total energy before collision is $E_1=\frac{1}{2} m u^2$ After collision, the energy gained by the deuteron is E_d=$\frac{1}{2} \times($2 m) v_2^2=m $\times\left(\frac{2}{3}$u\right)^2=$\frac{4}{9}$m u² . $E_d$ is the amount of energy lost by the neutron. Therefore the fractional loss of energy of the neutron is $\frac{E_d}{E_1}=\frac{(4 / 9) m u^2}{(1 / 2) m u^2}=\frac{8}{9}$

101426.subject: Physics
101426.text: Two point masses $m$ and $4m$ are separated by an unknown distance $r$. The gravitational potential at the point on the line joining them where the net gravitational field is zero, is found to be $-V_0$. The separation distance $r$ between the two masses is:
101426.sol:
Let the neutral point (where the net gravitational field is zero) be at a distance $x$ from the mass $m$.

Equating the magnitudes of the gravitational fields produced by both masses at this point:
$\dfrac{Gm}{x^2} = \dfrac{G(4m)}{(r-x)^2}$

Taking the square root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{2}{r-x}$
$\Rightarrow r - x = 2x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{r}{3}$

The distance of this neutral point from the mass $4m$ is $r - \dfrac{r}{3} = \dfrac{2r}{3}$.

The net gravitational potential $V$ at this point is the scalar sum of the potentials due to both masses:
$V = -\dfrac{Gm}{x} - \dfrac{G(4m)}{r-x}$
$V = -\dfrac{Gm}{\left(\dfrac{r}{3}\right)} - \dfrac{4Gm}{\left(\dfrac{2r}{3}\right)}$
$V = -\dfrac{3Gm}{r} - \dfrac{6Gm}{r} = -\dfrac{9Gm}{r}$

We are given that the potential at this point is $-V_0$. Therefore:
$-V_0 = -\dfrac{9Gm}{r}$
$\Rightarrow r = \dfrac{9Gm}{V_0}$

Answer: $\dfrac{9Gm}{V_0}$

[Given: $R = \dfrac{25}{3} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ and molar mass of $\mathrm{He} = 4 \mathrm{~g/mol}$]
102252.sol:
The total translational kinetic energy of an ideal gas is given by $E = \dfrac{3}{2}nRT$.

For the initial state ($T_1 = 127^{\circ} \mathrm{C} = 400 \mathrm{~K}$):
$n_1 = \dfrac{2E_1}{3RT_1} = \dfrac{2 \times 50000}{3 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right) \times 400} = \dfrac{100000}{25 \times 400} = 10 \mathrm{~mol}$

For the final state ($T_2 = 27^{\circ} \mathrm{C} = 300 \mathrm{~K}$):
$n_2 = \dfrac{2E_2}{3RT_2} = \dfrac{2 \times 15000}{3 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right) \times 300} = \dfrac{30000}{25 \times 300} = 4 \mathrm{~mol}$

Number of moles of Helium that escaped $= n_1 - n_2 = 10 - 4 = 6 \mathrm{~mol}$

Mass of escaped Helium $= \text{moles} \times \text{molar mass} = 6 \mathrm{~mol} \times 4 \mathrm{~g/mol} = 24 \mathrm{~g}$

Answer: $24 \mathrm{~g}$

102446.text: A body of mass $100$ g is executing simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $0.1$ m and a time period of $\pi$ seconds. The total mechanical energy of the oscillating system is :
102446.sol:
The total mechanical energy $E$ of a body executing simple harmonic motion is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2$

where $m$ is the mass, $\omega$ is the angular frequency, and $A$ is the amplitude.

Given:
Mass, $m = 100$ g $= 0.1$ kg
Amplitude, $A = 0.1$ m
Time period, $T = \pi$ s

First, calculate the angular frequency $\omega$:

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2$ rad/s

Now, substitute the values into the energy formula:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times (2)^2 \times (0.1)^2$

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times 4 \times 0.01$

$E = 0.2 \times 0.01 = 0.002$ J.

Answer: $0.002$ J

102459.subject: Physics
102459.text: Two cyclists A and B are moving with uniform circular motion on identical circular tracks. Cyclist A completes one revolution in 3 minutes, while cyclist B completes one revolution in 4 minutes. What is the ratio of the angular distances covered by A and B ($\theta_A : \theta_B$) in a time interval of 12 minutes?
102459.sol:
The angular distance covered by a particle in uniform circular motion is given by $\theta = \omega t = \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t$.
For cyclist A, the time period $T_A = 3 \text{ minutes}$.
For cyclist B, the time period $T_B = 4 \text{ minutes}$.
Since the time interval $t = 12 \text{ minutes}$ is the same for both cyclists, the ratio of their angular distances is inversely proportional to their time periods:
$\dfrac{\theta_A}{\theta_B} = \dfrac{T_B}{T_A}$
$\dfrac{\theta_A}{\theta_B} = \dfrac{4}{3}$
Thus, the ratio is $4 : 3$.

Answer: $4 : 3$

103343.subject: Physics
103343.text: A uniform wire AB of resistance $12\ \Omega$ is connected to a battery of EMF $26\ \text{V}$ and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$. A resistor $R = 12\ \Omega$ is connected between end A and a point C on the wire, such that the length AC is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the total length AB. What is the electrical power dissipated in the resistor $R$?
103343.sol:
The resistance of the wire is proportional to its length. The resistance of segment AC is $\dfrac{1}{3} \times 12\ \Omega = 4\ \Omega$, and the resistance of segment CB is $\dfrac{2}{3} \times 12\ \Omega = 8\ \Omega$.

The external resistor $R = 12\ \Omega$ is connected in parallel with the segment AC. The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is:
$R_{AC} = \dfrac{12 \times 4}{12 + 4} = \dfrac{48}{16} = 3\ \Omega$

The total resistance of the circuit includes $R_{AC}$, the remaining wire segment CB, and the internal resistance of the battery:
$R_{total} = R_{AC} + R_{CB} + r = 3\ \Omega + 8\ \Omega + 2\ \Omega = 13\ \Omega$

The total current drawn from the battery is:
$I = \dfrac{E}{R_{total}} = \dfrac{26\ \text{V}}{13\ \Omega} = 2\ \text{A}$

The potential difference across the parallel combination (segment AC and resistor $R$) is:
$V_{AC} = I \times R_{AC} = 2\ \text{A} \times 3\ \Omega = 6\ \text{V}$

The electrical power dissipated in the resistor $R$ is:
$P = \dfrac{V_{AC}^2}{R} = \dfrac{(6\ \text{V})^2}{12\ \Omega} = \dfrac{36}{12} = 3\ \text{W}$

Answer: $3\ \text{W}$
